title: Implement analytic functions
action: Translate the closed-form expressions for spring‑back ratio SR, critical loading factor α_c, and the lower‑limit inequality (as derived in the paper) into Python functions. These will be used in the subsequent computation steps.
description: This step prepares the computational model by implementing the necessary formulas. No scored artifact is produced.

title: Compute spring‑back ratio SR vs loading factor α
action: For each combination of fixed parameters (w/t, t/2ρ, n, μ, R, θ) and for loading factor α from 0 to 0.2 in steps of 0.01, evaluate the SR function. Write the results to sr_data.csv.
description: Compute the spring‑back ratio SR as a function of the loading factor α for all parameter combinations given in the output schema. This covers the equivalent of Figs 2–7 from the paper.
output_schema: columns: alpha (numeric), w_t (numeric), t_2rho (numeric), n (numeric), mu (numeric), R (numeric), theta (numeric), SR (numeric). The parameter grids are: w/t in [8, 14] step 2, t/2ρ in [0.05, 0.15] step 0.025, n in [0.1, 0.5] step 0.1, μ in [0.0, 0.2] step 0.1, R in [0.5, 2.0] step 0.5, θ in [30°, 60°] step 10°. Alpha ranges from 0 to 0.2 with step 0.01.

title: Compute critical loading factor α_c
action: For each combination of parameters (R, n, w/t, t/2ρ, μ, θ) from the specified grids, evaluate the α_c function that satisfies SR=0. Write the results to alpha_c_data.csv.
description: Compute the critical loading factor α_c that completely eliminates spring‑back. This covers the equivalent of Figs 8–10 from the paper.
output_schema: columns: R (numeric), n (numeric), w_t (numeric), t_2rho (numeric), mu (numeric), theta (numeric), alpha_c (numeric). Parameter ranges: R in [0.5, 2.0] step 0.5, n in [0.1, 0.5] step 0.1, w/t in [8, 14] step 2, t/2ρ in [0.05, 0.15] step 0.025, μ in [0.0, 0.2] step 0.1, θ in [30°, 60°] step 10°.

title: Compute lower limit of t/2ρ
action: For each combination of w/t and θ, compute the minimum allowed t/2ρ from the inequality l0/t > 0. Write the results to lower_limit_data.csv.
description: Compute the lower limit of the geometrical ratio t/2ρ for which the coining contact length remains positive. This covers the equivalent of Figs 11–12 from the paper.
output_schema: columns: w_t (numeric), theta (numeric), lower_limit (numeric). w/t in [8, 14] step 1, θ in [30°, 60°] step 5°.
